transcript.text:
There are two approaches, depending on whether you have admin access or are a non-admin looking up public attributes.

---

## Option 1: Search API (recommended for admins)

Send a `POST` to the search endpoint, filtering the `identities` index by the email attribute:

```http
POST https://{tenant}.api.identitynow.com/search/v1
Authorization: Bearer {access_token}
Content-Type: application/json

{
  "indices": ["identities"],
  "query": {
    "query": "attributes.email:\"jane.doe@example.com\""
  }
}
```

The search docs note that the query syntax supports field-specific searches like `attributes.location:austin` — the same pattern applies to `attributes.email`.

---

## Option 2: Public Identities API (works for non-admins)

The Public Identities API exposes a `filters` parameter and email is one of the default visible attributes:

```http
GET https://{tenant}.api.identitynow.com/public-identities/v1?filters=email eq "jane.doe@example.com"
Authorization: Bearer {access_token}
```

---

## Authentication

For either call, first get an access token via the client credentials grant:

```bash
curl -X POST \
  'https://{tenant}.api.identitynow.com/oauth/token' \
  --form 'grant_type="client_credentials"' \
  --form 'client_id="{clientId}"' \
  --form 'client_secret="{clientSecret}"'
```

Then use the returned `access_token` in your `Authorization: Bearer {access_token}` header.

---

**Which to use:** The Search API gives richer identity data and works best for admins/scripts. The Public Identities API is simpler and appropriate when you only need publicly visible attributes or are operating in a non-admin context.

```answer-summary
endpoints:
  - method: POST
    path: /search/v1
    api_version: search/v1
  - method: GET
    path: /public-identities/v1
    api_version: public-identities/v1
auth_flow: OAuth2 bearer token
required_scopes: []
key_parameters: [indices, query, filters]
```
